{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4221e11ac09016034e04b576f7c846e2829d4e3cfe8e850c8ca89ddcfc32ddcf","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:78","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Graduated driver license summary","heading":"C — Graduated driver license summary","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Graduated driver license summary

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A86
Alabama's graduated driver license rules do not apply to anyone 18 years of age or older. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A86
They also do not apply to a 17-year-old or older driver who has held a valid license for 6 months or more. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A86
A person 16 or older who is married or is the head of a household is exempt from the graduated rules. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A86
Someone who has been legally relieved of minority status is also outside the graduated rules. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A86
A person under 18 cannot apply for an unrestricted license until holding a learner license for at least six months with no restriction violations, and must be 17. [A86]
Why it matters: six months on the learner license is not enough by itself; the applicant must also have reached 17.
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A86
A fifteen-year-old holding a valid learner license may drive only when a parent, legal guardian, licensed driver aged twenty-one or older, or licensed or certified driving instructor occupies the front seat beside the driver [A86].
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A86
A licensed or certified driving instructor sitting in the front seat beside the 15-year-old also satisfies the supervision rule. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A86
A 16-year-old needs a parent's or legal guardian's permission both to get a license and to drive without supervision. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A86
The license restrictions apply to drivers who are 16, and to 17-year-olds who have held a license for less than 6 months. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A86
A restricted driver may carry no more than 1 nonfamily passenger besides the parent, guardian or supervising licensed driver aged at least 21, a limit cut from four in 2010. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A86
A restricted driver may not drive between 12 midnight and 6 a.m. unless a parent or legal guardian is along or an exception applies. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A86
A restricted young driver may not operate a vehicle from midnight to six a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian, riding with a licensed driver twenty-one or older with parental consent, traveling to or from regular work or a school- or religious-sponsored event, or driving for a medical, fire, or law-enforcement emergency [A86].
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A86
Late-night driving is also allowed when going to or from the driver's regular workplace, a school-sponsored event or a religious-sponsored event. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A86
The restrictions also bar driving while using any handheld communication device, and violating that rule extends the graduated period and/or suspends the license. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A86
Breaking a graduated-license condition is a traffic violation but carries no criminal penalty or court costs. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A86
A citation for a graduated-license violation is issued only when the driver is stopped and cited for a separate violation of the law. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A86
No points go on the record for violating the graduated-license restrictions. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A86
Any restriction violation extends the restricted period by 6 months or until the driver turns 18. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A86
A restricted driver's license is automatically suspended for 60 days after a second moving violation conviction or any conviction worth four or more points. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A86
The same 60-day suspension follows a conviction for failing to give information or render aid, racing, fleeing or eluding an officer, reckless driving, illegal passing or driving on the wrong side. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A86
The summary names the graduated license law as Act #02-408, with 2010 amendments effective 7/1/2010. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0086]

Glossary: graduated driver license — Alabama's staged licensing with restrictions for 15-, 16- and 17-year-old drivers [A86]. Restricted period — the stage during which the passenger, late-night and handheld-device limits apply [A86]. Relieved of minority status — legally treated as no longer below the legal age [A86].
Memory aid: one friend, no phone, home by midnight [A86].
